original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Does the sharp A8 simplex nine-term COPY floor 72 of research/a8-simplex-decoder-floor (#1248) survive arbitrary nonlinear zero-error messages with the same fixed supports, without and with free orthogonal side information at the readers, on #1248's two pinned sharp witnesses?
scope_change_reason: PR #5299 (research/a7-a1-nonlinear-copy-floor) poses this as its second Open next question: its no-side-information lemma transfers at once and its side-information lemma needs a separate A8 witness search. This package supplies that search; it does not synthesize a decoder or profile.
bottleneck_link: Side result: no new kappa. Removes nonlinear message coding and free orthogonal side information as routes to cheaper COPY on the two sharp A8 simplex witnesses.
stop_rule: Stop after finite side-information certificates on both pinned sharp witnesses; do not search all shift assignments under side information.
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the A8 model, binds both pinned sharp witnesses to the predecessor CERTIFICATE.json, and certifies per term an invertible fooling block of size rho_k and an induced Petersen+(rho_k-5) or rho_k-line non-orthogonal witness, totals 72 each; the exact independence bound alone totals 64; test_verify.py has twelve rejecting controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the orthogonal-side-information floor stay at 72 for every complex row shift of the A8 simplex decoder, not only the two sharp witnesses?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With free orthogonal side information a small demand graph can let even a linear code fall below its term's pairing rank; a shift with small supports would then change the copy contract.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a deficiency argument for broadcast rates of induced orthogonality subgraphs over the full shift family, analogous to #1248's 43,435-plane census.
open_questions.first_step: For each line list its support-reducing shifts and compute, per term, the largest demand set with no Petersen+(rank-5) witness and no rank-sized non-orthogonal set.

open_questions.question: Is the Petersen step forced for every rank-9 term, or would a different small induced subgraph with broadcast rate above its independence number also serve?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Each 50-line rank-9 demand graph has largest non-orthogonal set 8, so the plain independence bound loses one unit per term; a catalogue of rate-above-independence subgraphs would make side-information certificates portable to other frames.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such catalogue for the E8 orthogonality graph is checked here.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate induced subgraphs of one 50-line demand graph up to symmetry and compare fractional-clique-cover or LP bounds with the independence number.
